audit_findings.title: The anchor includes earnings from a business no longer owned
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.3 million FY2025 pre-tax disposal-group profit, equal to 2.5% of the $93.2 million anchor; exact owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-divestiture OE anchor still includes CFP operating profit, depreciation, working-capital movements and capital expenditures generated before its September 2025 sale.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended January 3, 2026 and December 28, 2024, pre-tax profit of the disposal group was $ 2.3 and $ 4.5 respectively, excluding the reclassification of CTA.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filing provides only CFP pre-tax profit, not the cash-flow components needed to measure its contribution to owner earnings. The disclosed profit is small relative to the anchor, but unreported working-capital and capital-spending effects prevent a supported conclusion that the valuation impact is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2025 OE excluding CFP revenue, operating costs, D&A, working-capital movements and capital expenditures, while keeping the sale gain and proceeds excluded from operating OE and treated correctly in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Actual-year capital spending may be below sustainable requirements
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed total-spending sensitivity of $31.5-$39.9 million, or $7.8-$16.2 million above FY2025 capex, by applying 3.75%-4.75% to $839.0 million sales; maintenance-only difference unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher recurring maintenance-capex deduction lowers anchor OE and every forecast cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital expenditures for 2026 are forecasted to be approximately 3.75% to 4.75% of sales for improvements to manufacturing technology and maintaining and replacing existing machine capabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential difference equals approximately 8%-17% of the $93.2 million anchor and therefore could materially reduce estimated value. The first half of 2026 also shows $18.0 million of capex, or 3.9% of sales. However, management's range includes manufacturing improvements and organic-growth investments as well as maintenance, so the record does not establish how much belongs in maintenance OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain maintenance, replacement, growth and capitalized-software spending by project; rerun all scenarios using normalized maintenance capex rather than total forecast capex.

audit_findings.title: A terminated-swap gain reduced anchor-year interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.4 million pre-tax and $4.2 million after tax as filed; the after-tax amount equals 4.5% of the $93.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model retaining interest expense, an unremoved nonrecurring reduction of interest expense increases anchor OE and its capitalized DCF value.
audit_findings.evidence: At January 3, 2026 , $ 5.4 was amortized from accumulated other comprehensive income into earnings as a reduction of interest expense with the remaining $ 1.7 to be amortized in 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring interest benefit is demonstrated, but the supplied valuation record does not show whether the OE calculator separately removed it. If retained, the filed after-tax amount would produce an approximately $1.75-per-share base-case overstatement using the supplied base operating-PV-to-anchor relationship; if already normalized, there is no remaining error.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $5.4 million reclassification through the anchor calculation and, if present, remove its $4.2 million filed after-tax effect before rerunning every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains a 53rd week
audit_findings.magnitude: One week, or 1.89% of the 53-week period; a pro-rata sensitivity is $1.76 million of anchor OE and approximately $0.73 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: The extra week can elevate the recurring OE base and thereby every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 fiscal year contained 53 weeks and ended January 3, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The 53rd week is demonstrated. A straight pro-rata normalization would reduce base value from $40.86 to approximately $40.13 per share, only $0.73 compared with the $30.76 gap between base value and the $71.62 market price. Seasonality could change the exact effect, but an ordinary extra-week adjustment is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the actual sales, costs, working capital and capex attributable to the extra week; normalize them if readily available, but no conclusion-level rerun is required unless that week was abnormally profitable.

audit_findings.title: A mandatory building purchase may be an unmodeled senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: €27.0 million gross purchase price less 60% of lease payments made before purchase; net claim unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If the agreement becomes binding, the eventual purchase consumes cash or increases financing needs unless funded through forecast reinvestment deductions.
audit_findings.evidence: The agreement includes an option to purchase during the lease period with a commitment to purchase at the end of the 6-year lease period.
audit_findings.explanation: The 10-K describes a draft agreement still under negotiation, while the July 2026 10-Q no longer reports the building commitment in its commitments note. The record therefore does not establish a present obligation or current valuation error. It remains a prospective capital-allocation risk that could enter OE or the equity bridge if executed.
audit_findings.action: Monitor subsequent filings and obtain the executed agreement, lease credits, commencement date, accounting treatment and funding plan; rerun OE or the bridge only if a binding net purchase obligation is established.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may carry repatriation friction
audit_findings.magnitude: $68.0 million bridge cash and $52.6 million of filed indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings; complete removal of the $68.0 million would reduce value by $2.02 per share and base value to $38.84
audit_findings.mechanism: Taxes, restrictions or minimum operating-cash requirements would reduce the cash added dollar-for-dollar in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 3, 2026, the Company had approximately $ 52.6 million of undistributed earnings in certain non-U.S. subsidiaries for which no deferred income taxes have been recorded.
audit_findings.explanation: Accessibility and incremental tax are unresolved, and the $52.6 million of undistributed earnings cannot be equated directly with the $68.0 million cash balance. Nevertheless, even the deliberately conservative removal of all bridge cash reduces each scenario by only $2.02 per share, leaving the $38.84 base and $43.37 bull values well below the $71.62 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map the $68.0 million by entity and jurisdiction and calculate withholding, state tax and minimum operating-cash requirements; adjust the bridge if identified, without reopening the overall conclusion.
